hrvMeasure.title: Measure HRV
hrvMeasure.prompt: Sit down, rest your arm, watch snug.
hrvMeasure.howBody: Wear the watch snug, about a finger above the wrist bone. Stay still and quiet for the whole minute; moving or talking spoils the reading. Live heart rate pauses meanwhile.
hrvMeasure.caveat: A single minute is a rough reading: posture, breathing and the time of day move it. Measure under the same conditions to compare.

sleep.detailsNaps: The percentage counts the whole day: this sleep plus naps that ended the same day.
sleep.detailsNeedStrain: Need is 7 h 30 min plus extra after a strain of {{strain}} that day.

noStages.title: Why does this sleep have no stages?
noStages.unsupported: The watch told us when you slept but not the stages, and it has no TruSleep switch that JoyoFit can set.
noStages.turnOn: Turn on TruSleep so the watch records sleep stages, then sleep a night and sync.
noStages.unknown: The watch told us when you slept but not the stages. Newer watches send them with TruSleep on. Some older ones cannot, and may give light and deep sleep with TruSleep off instead.

fitness.title: Fitness

hrvHint.balanced: Your HRV over the last 7 nights is inside your normal range.
hrvHint.low: Your HRV over the last 7 nights is below your normal range. Usually a sign of fatigue, too little sleep or illness.
hrvHint.unbalanced: Your HRV over the last 7 nights is above your normal range. Often seen after illness or a break from training.

hrvMissing.recent: {{have}} of {{need}} nights in the last 7 days

productive.hint: This week's load is above your usual: fitness is building.

maintaining.hint: This week's load matches your usual.

recovery.hint: This week's load is lighter than usual.

overreaching.hint: Load jumped sharply. Give your body time to recover.

detraining.hint: Load is well below your usual: fitness may drop.

fitness.noSleep: No sleep data for last night yet. Wear the watch to bed, then sync.

today.howEnergy: A JoyoFit estimate, not a watch figure. Wake-up level = 30 + 60 x (your sleep / sleep need, at most 1) + up to 10 points from overnight HRV. It then drops 0.8 per hour awake, up to 55 points from strain since waking, and up to 1 point per hour when stress is above 40. It rises 5 per hour of naps and 0.4 per hour of resting with a heart rate near your resting rate. The result is capped between 0 and 100.
today.howEnergyNow: Right now: wake-up {{wake}}, awake {{awake}}, strain {{strain}}, stress {{stress}}, naps {{naps}}, rest {{rest}}.
today.recoveryNone: No workouts or heart rate data yet
today.howRecoveryWatch: From the watch: the recovery time of the latest workout the watch reported, counted down from when the workout ended. With several workouts, the longest one is used.
today.howRecoveryEstimate: A JoyoFit estimate: the watch gave no recovery time, so it is worked out from today's and yesterday's strain. Below strain 5 there is no recovery time, at strain 5 about 6 hours, rising in a straight line to 48 hours at strain 21. Yesterday's strain counts down from midnight.
today.howNeed: A JoyoFit estimate: a base of 7 h 30 min, plus up to 1 hour from today's strain (strain / 21), plus a quarter of the sleep debt of the last 7 nights (the shortfall from 7 h 30 min a night), at most 1 hour.
today.howNeedNoDebt: Sleep debt is not counted yet: it needs at least 3 recorded nights.
today.navSubtitle: VO2max, training status, race predictions, HRV, intensity minutes

vo2.title: VO2max
vo2.none: No VO2max yet. The watch reports it after a run or GPS walk, or JoyoFit estimates it from your resting heart rate after 5 recorded days.
vo2.how: From the watch: the VO2max the watch reported on the latest workout (90 days). The watch sends maximum METs; JoyoFit multiplies by 3.5 ml/kg/min per MET and rounds down to a whole number, so it can be 1 below the watch's figure. Values outside 10 to 90 are ignored. Estimate (when the watch reports none): Uth-Sorensen 2004, VO2max = 15.3 x maximum heart rate / resting heart rate. Maximum is 220 minus the age from your profile, resting is the median of the daily lowest heart rates of the last 14 days. Rough: the real figure can be off by a few points.

load.title: Training status
load.short_one: Needs at least {{need}} days with stored heart rate: only {{count}} day so far.
load.short_other: Needs at least {{need}} days with stored heart rate: only {{count}} days so far.
load.none: No training load in the last 28 days.
load.how: A JoyoFit estimate from the heart rate the watch stored. Daily load = Edwards TRIMP (minutes in zones 1 to 5 times 1 to 5). Ratio = mean TRIMP of the last 7 days divided by the mean of the last 28 days (Gabbett 2016), today excluded. Above 1.5 is overreaching, 1.1 to 1.5 productive, 0.8 to 1.1 maintaining, 0.5 to 0.8 recovery, below 0.5 detraining. The same figure feeds Readiness. Days without data count as rest.

races.title: Race predictions
races.note: An estimate, from your best efforts in runs of the last 90 days.
races.short_one: Needs at least {{need}} runs of 5 km or more in the last 90 days (GPS): only {{count}} so far.
races.short_other: Needs at least {{need}} runs of 5 km or more in the last 90 days (GPS): only {{count}} so far.
races.how: A JoyoFit estimate with Riegel's formula (1981): T2 = T1 x (D2 / D1)^1.06. T1 is your fastest 5K, 10K or half marathon effort from runs of the last 90 days (the same as the best efforts in workout details). Each distance uses the effort closest to it. A marathon from a 5K effort tends to be too optimistic if you have not trained long runs.

hrv.title: HRV status
hrv.iosFallback: Night HRV is not read on iPhone yet
hrv.how: A JoyoFit estimate from the overnight HRV (RMSSD) the watch records while you sleep, Android only. The mean ln(RMSSD) of the last 7 nights is compared with your normal range: the mean of the 60 days before that week, plus or minus 1 standard deviation (Plews 2013, Buchheit 2014). Inside the range: balanced. Below: low. Above: unbalanced. Needs 14 baseline nights and 3 nights in the last 7 days.

intensity.title: Intensity minutes
intensity.headline: This week, target {{target}} minutes
intensity.breakdown: {{moderate}} moderate minutes + 2 x {{vigorous}} vigorous minutes. Estimate.
intensity.chart: Intensity minutes per day, Monday to Sunday
intensity.how: A JoyoFit estimate from the per-minute heart rate the watch stored (maximum {{maxHr}} bpm). Minutes at 60 to 80 percent of maximum (zones 2 and 3) count 1, minutes at 80 percent and above (zones 4 and 5) count 2. The week runs Monday to Sunday. The target of 150 minutes a week follows WHO 2020 and ACSM 2018 advice.
